content.introduction: The latest stock market news indicates modest gains with seven S&P 500 sectors finishing higher, although the gains were relatively modest. Decliners outpaced advancers by a slim 7-to-6 margin on the NYSE, while advancers held a roughly 4-to-3 edge on the Nasdaq. The consumer discretionary sector finished unchanged, while the utilities, real estate, and consumer staples sectors lagged. Macroeconomic developments were significant, with the FOMC leaving interest rates unchanged while crude oil prices surged amid renewed geopolitical concerns about Iran. WTI crude futures settled $2.87 higher (+2.9%) at $102.74 per barrel.
body:
Participation had a positive tilt, with seven S&P 500 sectors finishing higher, although gains remained relatively modest. Decliners outpaced advancers by a slim 7-to-6 margin on the NYSE, while advancers held a roughly 4-to-3 edge on the Nasdaq.

The consumer discretionary sector finished unchanged, while the utilities (-0.9%), real estate (-0.7%), and consumer staples (-0.4%) sectors lagged. The weakness in rate-sensitive areas came as Treasury yields climbed alongside crude oil prices. [...] Macroeconomic developments commanded considerable attention, with the FOMC leaving interest rates unchanged while reinforcing its commitment to bringing inflation back to target. Meanwhile, crude oil prices surged amid renewed concerns about a potential escalation in the conflict with Iran, contributing to upward pressure on Treasury yields and creating an additional headwind for the broader market. [...] WTI crude futures settled $2.87 higher (+2.9%) at $102.74 per barrel amid renewed geopolitical concerns. According to _Axios_, regional mediators led by Qatar are pressing Iran for nuclear concessions as the possibility of U.S. military strikes following the midterm elections looms in the absence of an agreement.
